# Mahāsaccaka Sutta (MN 36 (PTS MN i 237))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In later Sri Lankan tradition, the text was selected by Mahinda to be rehearsed by Mahārittha at the Thūpārāma assembly [Buswell & Lopez 2014].
DharmaNexus also confirms extensive Pali-internal text reuse: the sutta shares large textual sequences (often exceeding 90,000 characters) with other autobiographical accounts in the *Majjhimanikāya*, particularly the *Saṅgārava Sutta* (MN 100), the *Bodhirājakumāra Sutta* (MN 85), and the *Pāsarāsi Sutta* (MN 26) [DharmaNexus].
